Suppose $X_1, \ldots, X_n \siid \ndist{\mu, \sigma^2}$,
and let $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ be the observed values.
The parameter vector is $\vth = (\mu, \sigma^2)$.
We treat $\sigma^2$, rather than $\sigma$, as the second parameter,
and differentiate with respect to $\sigma^2$ directly.

By @thm-lik-iid, the likelihood is:

$$
\Lik(\mu, \sigma^2) = \prod_{i=1}^n (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/2}
\expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}
$$

and by @thm-loglik-iid, the log-likelihood is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell(\mu, \sigma^2)
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{-\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\sigma^2} - \frac{(x_i - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}
&& \text{(log of each Gaussian density)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}
 - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(split the sum; log of a product)}
\end{aligned}
$$
